sections.overview: The Northern Bluet is a widespread North American damselfly, ranging across much of the Nearctic.
sections.identification: Adults are about 29–40 mm long; the abdomen is mostly blue with black markings, but close inspection may be needed to separate it from similar bluets.
sections.habitat: It uses still waters such as ponds; Virginia records cited by the state atlas are from high-elevation beaver ponds.
sections.diet: The species accounts consulted give no prey list for the Northern Bluet.
sections.behavior: Similar bluets can require close examination to identify reliably.
sections.reproduction: The consulted accounts provide flight dates but little detail on courtship or egg-laying.
sections.ecology: Compare Enallagma carunculatum and Enallagma signatum: the former has more black on the male abdomen, while the latter is orange.
sections.conservation: NatureServe ranks the species globally secure (G5); that broad rank does not mean every local population is equally common.
